subject: Pilot environment: infra readiness and next steps
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@orchidanalytics.com>, Jamie Li <jamie.li@orchidanalytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot environment: infra readiness and next steps

Thanks for a productive call earlier — quick recap and actions so we have alignment for the pilot environment: 

Decisions we captured:
- Pilot will run in Orchid Analytics' AWS account in us-west-2.
- Target pilot start: 2027-04-20; target completion and go/no-go review: 2027-05-04.

Immediate infra dependencies (owners + asks):
1) VPC peering & routing (Owner: Orchid infra / Jamie)
   - Provide VPC IDs, CIDR ranges, expected egress IPs for NAT/egress.
   - Confirm whether route propagation is allowed for peer; if not, we need a short-lived NAT gateway config.
2) IP allowlist (Owner: Orchid security / security@orchidanalytics.com)
   - We'll supply a list of Redwood egress IPs. Please confirm firewall maintenance windows for the peering IP entries.
3) SSO / SAML (Owner: Orchid IdP / Alex)
   - Send SAML metadata (IdP) and preferred attribute mapping (email, name, groups).
   - Redwood can consume either raw XML or a metadata URL.
4) Secrets / KMS (Owner: Orchid security / Karthik to coordinate)
   - If you can provide a customer-managed KMS key ARN for envelope encryption, please share the ARN or grant Redwood service principal the Encrypt/Decrypt on a test key.
   - If a full KMS share is not allowed, we can use Redwood-managed keys and rotate secrets via a short-term process.

Risks / blockers:
- Firewall change window: if peering requires firewall approval more than 5 business days out, pilot start will slip.
- KMS policy approvals can take time for regulated workloads — we flagged this with our onboarding team.

Attachments: network_diagram_v2.pdf (high-level subnet/peering diagram)

Next steps & dates:
- By 2027-04-12: Orchid to share VPC IDs, initial SAML metadata, and preferred contact for firewall. (Alex/Jamie)
- By 2027-04-14: Redwood to produce MAP draft with milestones + responsibilities. (Ben)
- 2027-04-15: 30-min sync to validate peering plan and allowlist window.

If anyone prefers a different owner mapping, call it out and we’ll update the MAP.

Thanks — I’ll circulate the MAP draft once Ben sends the baseline.

--
Irene Choi
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@orchidanalytics.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jamie Li <jamie.li@orchidanalytics.com>, Orchid Analytics Security <security@orchidanalytics.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 18:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot environment: infra readiness and next steps

Thanks, Irene — good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- We can provide VPC IDs and CIDRs by COB Monday (2027-04-12). Expect two VPCs: prod-analytics-vpc (10.10.0.0/16) and sandbox-pilot-vpc (10.20.0.0/16).
- Security requests that Redwood share the list of egress IPs you intend to use so we can pre-seed the firewall change request.
- SAML metadata: attaching the current metadata XML (saml-metadata.xml). We use Okta and will send an attributes sheet in a follow-up.
- KMS: Our security team prefers customer-managed keys. We cannot share the production key ARN publicly, but we can create a test CMK for the pilot and grant Redwood the required permissions. Karthik is looped in to finalize permissions.

Attachment: saml-metadata.xml

We’ll aim to have the firewall change window confirmed by 2027-04-13. If any approvals are slower, we’ll escalate internally.

Alex
Head of Platform Engineering | Orchid Analytics
alex.morgan@orchidanalytics.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Draft MAP: pilot connectivity & secrets milestone (attached)

Folks — I put together a short MAP slice focused on connectivity, SSO, and secrets for the pilot. High level below; full draft attached (map_draft.xlsx).

MAP (connectivity / secrets slice):
- Milestone A (VPC peering established): Target date 2027-04-18
  - Owner: Orchid (Jamie) to provide VPC IDs and submit peering request.
  - Redwood (Ben) to create peering config and shared routing plan.
  - Dependency: Firewall allowlist entry scheduled

- Milestone B (IP allowlist & egress validation): Target date 2027-04-18
  - Owner: Orchid Security (security@orchidanalytics.com) to approve rules.
  - Redwood to run egress validation and confirm packet flows.

- Milestone C (SSO configured): Target date 2027-04-19
  - Owner: Orchid IdP (Alex) to provide metadata + attribute mapping.
  - Redwood (Monica) to validate SAML assertion attributes and create pilot users.

- Milestone D (Secrets & KMS access): Target date 2027-04-19
  - Owner: Orchid Security / Karthik to approve test CMK permissions.
  - Redwood Ops to demonstrate envelope encryption using the test CMK.

Risks & contingency:
- If firewall takes >5 business days, shift pilot start by 1 week.
- If CMK policy reviews delay, Redwood can use Redwood-managed keys for an initial run while policy completes.

Please review the attached spreadsheet which maps owners, Jira ticket IDs (we’ll create after you sign off), and a short acceptance criteria column. If this reflects reality, reply-all with "ACK MAP slice" and we’ll lock milestones and create the Jira tasks.

Attachment: map_draft.xlsx

Thanks — I’ll schedule the 30-min follow-up for 2027-04-15 once we have the VPC IDs.

--
Ben Carter
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

ACK MAP slice.

We’ll send the VPC IDs Monday morning and the firewall maintenance window confirmation by Tue 2027-04-13. Karthik — I’ll work with your team on a test CMK policy; Jamie will be the owner for the peering request.

Let’s keep the 2027-04-15 30-min sync on the calendar (Irene, Ben: can you propose two windows?)

Thanks — Alex
